recs.title: VLSP 2025 Shared Task: Vietnamese Temporal Question Answering (TemporalQA)
recs.venue: VNU Journal of Science Computer Science and Communication Engineering
recs.summary: This task aims to benchmark systems in their ability to comprehend and perform reasoning over temporal information expressed in Vietnamese, providing the first dedicated benchmark for temporal reasoning in Vietnamese, filling animportant resource gap and supporting future research on temporal understanding and reasoning for Vietnamese NLP.

recs.title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?
recs.summary: A combined approach is proposed that fine-tunes the model while taking KV cache concatenation into account and selectively recomputes a subset of the KV caches and demonstrates improved accuracy for long-context inputs.

recs.title: NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction
recs.summary: NCP-ArchPreview is introduced, a latent-space language model that pushes autoregressive pretraining beyond standard next-token prediction (NTP) and learns through Next Concept Prediction (NCP) to predict discrete concepts that span multiple tokens, introducing an explicit and more challenging concept-level objective while preserving standard token-level autoregressive generation.

recs.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
recs.summary: This work introduces answer-distribution trajectories, a stochastic-dynamics-inspired representation that tracks the model's full predictive distribution over answers as reasoning unfolds, and suggests that answer-distribution trajectories provide a rich framework for analysing and evaluating the dynamics of LLM reasoning.

recs.title: TROVE: Adaptive Agent Skill Orchestration via Trace-Grounded Route Validation and Editing
recs.summary: Evaluation across code-generation, question-answering, and math reasoning benchmarks with different LLM backbones show that TROVE delivers a stronger quality-efficiency trade-off than existing baselines of dataset-level optimization, query-level architecture selection, and graph-constrained scheduling.

recs.title: RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory
recs.summary: RecurTrace introduces Loop Memory Attention, which lets each looped layer attend to its own states from previous iterations along the loop-time axis, so the model can revisit earlier computations instead of relying on the latest state alone.

recs.title: Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
recs.summary: Codebook Agent is the most accurate method on all six benchmarks the authors compare, and an MLP proxy that reads the flattened adjacency, regressed on measured utility and per-task normalized token cost, reranks the top decoded candidates in a single batched forward pass.

recs.title: AgentFactory: Towards Automated Agentic System Design and Optimization
recs.venue: Pacific Rim International Conference on Artificial Intelligence
recs.summary: AgentFactory is presented, a framework that jointly optimizes both foundation models and workflow structures in agentic systems while considering multiple objectives including performance, cost, and efficiency, and establishes AgentFactory as a promising approach for developing more capable and efficient agentic systems through automated optimization.

recs.title: TuringLLM: Efficiently Scaling Foundation Models Toward Physical AI
recs.summary: Despite its compact active-parameter budget, Turing-20B-A2B achieves, at the base-model stage, overall general capability exceeding Qwen3-8B Base and approaching Qwen3.5-9B Base, while maintaining strong long-context performance and favorable prefill-latency scaling.

recs.title: Beneath the Diff: Diagnosing and Mitigating Algorithmic Mode Collapse in Code-Level Autonomous Research Loops
recs.summary: This work identifies a robust failure mode that is accompanied by a widening gap between in-loop metric gains and gains measured on independent held-out evaluations and proposes Diversity-Aware Proposal Sampling (DAPS), a lightweight mitigation that combines category-coverage reweighting, persistent edit memory, and a validation gate.

recs.title: CONE: Embeddings for Complex Numerical Data Preserving Unit and Variable Semantics
recs.summary: This paper proposes CONE, a hybrid transformer encoder pre-trained model that encodes numbers, ranges, and gaussians into an embedding vector space preserving distance and introduces a novel composite embedding construction algorithm that integrates numerical values, ranges or gaussians together with their associated units and attribute names to precisely capture their intricate semantics.

recs.title: NumColBERT: Non-Intrusive Numeracy Injection for Late-Interaction Retrieval Models
recs.venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
recs.summary: Experimental results show that NumColBERT substantially outperforms standard fine-tuning baselines and achieves accuracy that matches or exceeds that of prior approaches that rely on separate textual and numerical scoring.

recs.title: GenBERTplus : A New Approach to Numeracy in Natural Language Processing
Toten: A Knowledge-Based System For Structure-Preserving Representation Of Physical Quantities And Technical Notation In Brazilian Portuguese
recs.summary: This work presents TOTEN, a knowledge-based system whose input representation preserves each technical entity as a whole, typed unit: vocabulary is not derived statistically but classified declaratively under a formal ontology of engineering entities (OEE).

recs.title: How Much Is One Recurrence Worth? Iso-Depth Scaling Laws for Looped Language Models
recs.summary: The utility of $\varphi$ is demonstrated as a diagnostic tool on two case studies, indicating that the loop mechanism is poorly trained under truncation, even though validation loss decreases.

recs.title: RMA: an Agentic System for Research-Level Mathematical Problems
recs.summary: Through comprehensive expert evaluation, RMA outperforms strong baselines on the First Proof benchmark, including GPT-5.2R and Aletheia, solving eight out of ten research problems and producing more logically sound and readable proofs.

recs.title: Pt-HotpotQA: Evaluating Multi-Hop Question Answering on Original and Portuguese-translated Datasets Using LLMs
recs.venue: Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society
recs.summary: It is demonstrated that multilingual models consistently perform better in English than in Portuguese, though this gap narrows with increased model size, and the impact of fine-tuning on improving MHQA performance in Portuguese is shown.

recs.title: DashAttention: Differentiable and Adaptive Sparse Hierarchical Attention
recs.summary: This work proposes DashAttention (Differentiable and Adaptive Sparse Hierarchical Attention), which leverages the adaptively sparse $\alpha$-entmax transformation to select a variable number of blocks according to the current query in the first stage, keeping the entire hierarchy fully differentiable.

recs.title: FRAME: Learning the Adaptation Domain with a Mixture of Fractional-Fourier Experts
recs.summary: Fractional-Fourier Mixture of Experts improves over strong MoE-LoRA and spectral baselines -- including FlyLoRA, FourierMoE, and HMoRA -- while keeping the active-parameter budget small, and analysis shows that the learned orders specialize by task and layer in interpretable ways.

recs.title: The Routing Plateau: Understanding and Breaking the Accuracy Limits of LLM Routers
recs.summary: This investigation shows that the plateau is largely caused by a predictability bottleneck: current routers mainly learn global averaged model-performance trends rather than fine-grained query-specific routing signals, and that larger training datasets, stronger encoders, and end-to-end fine-tuning can further improve routing accuracy.

recs.title: Analysing Mathematical Reasoning Abilities of Neural Models
recs.summary: This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of models from two broad classes of the most powerful sequence-to-sequence architectures and finds notable differences in their ability to resolve mathematical problems and generalize their knowledge.

recs.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
recs.summary: It is found that how a number is represented in its surface form has a strong influence on the model's accuracy, and this result bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.

recs.title: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: An approach to infer relative physical knowledge of actions and objects along five dimensions (e.g., size, weight, and strength) from unstructured natural language text is presented.

recs.title: Investigating Numeracy Learning Ability of a Text-to-Text Transfer Model
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work investigates the ability of text-to-text transfer learning model (T5), which has outperformed its predecessors in the conventional NLP tasks, to learn numeracy, to struggle considerably in the extrapolation setting across all four tasks.

recs.title: Measuring Arithmetic Extrapolation Performance
recs.summary: It is found that consistently learning arithmetic extrapolation is challenging, in particular for multiplication, in the first extensive evaluation with respect to convergence of the NALU and its sub-units.

recs.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
recs.summary: Two novel model architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from very large data sets are proposed and it is shown that these vectors provide state-of-the-art performance on the authors' test set for measuring syntactic and semantic word similarities.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: WordNet: A Lexical Database for English
recs.venue: Human Language Technology - The Baltic Perspectiv
recs.summary: WordNet1 provides a more effective combination of traditional lexicographic information and modern computing, and is an online lexical database designed for use under program control.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: The self-organizing map
recs.summary: The self-organizing map, an architecture suggested for artificial neural networks, is explained by presenting simulation experiments and practical applications, and an algorithm which order responses spatially is reviewed, focusing on best matching cell selection and adaptation of the weight vectors.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Children's understanding of counting.
recs.summary: Children learn the meanings of smaller number words before larger ones within their counting range, up to the number three or four, indicating that children learn the cardinal word principle at roughly 3 1/2 years of age.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
recs.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: The topmost weight matrix of neural network language models is studied and it is shown that this matrix constitutes a valid word embedding and a new method of regularizing the output embedding is offered.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Variability signatures distinguish verbal from nonverbal counting for both large and small numbers
recs.summary: The unexpected power-law relation between target value and mean number of presses in nonverbal counting suggests a new hypothesis about the development of the function relating number symbols to mental magnitudes.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: EFFECTIVE TEACHERS OF NUMERACY
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Core systems in human cognition.
recs.summary: Research on human infants, adult nonhuman primates, and children and adults in diverse cultures provides converging evidence for four systems at the foundations of human knowledge.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Leap-Of-Thought: Teaching Pre-Trained Models to Systematically Reason Over Implicit Knowledge
recs.summary: This work provides a first demonstration that LMs can be trained to reliably perform systematic reasoning combining both implicit, pre-trained knowledge and explicit natural language statements, and demonstrates that models learn to effectively perform inference which involves implicit taxonomic and world knowledge, chaining and counting.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing Proceedings of the Fourth International Workshop on Natural Language Processing for Social Media Socialnlp@emnlp2016 Chairs' Welcome Identifying and Categorizing Disaster-related Tweets Why Do They Leave: Modeling Participation in Online
recs.summary: This paper presents a system for classifying disaster-related tweets, and proposes an annotation schema for identifying relevant tweets as well as the more fine-grained categories they represent, and develop feature-rich classifiers for relevance and fine- grained categorization.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: From 'F' to 'A' on the N.Y. Regents Science Exams: An Overview of the Aristo Project
recs.summary: Success is reported on the Grade 8 New York Regents Science Exam, where for the first time a system scores more than 90 percent on the exam’s nondiagram, multiple choice (NDMC) questions, demonstrating that modern natural language processing methods can result in mastery on this task.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: On the Computational Power of Transformers and Its Implications in Sequence Modeling
recs.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
recs.summary: This paper provides an alternate and simpler proof to show that vanilla Transformers are Turing-complete and proves that Transformers with only positional masking and without any positional encoding are also Turing- complete.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test.
recs.summary: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test (BCET), a 20-item test with five estimation questions in each of four categories: time/duration, quantity, weight, and distance, indicated that the BCET was able to distinguish between demented and intact elderly participants.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: “Was It Good? It Was Provocative.” Learning the Meaning of Scalar Adjectives
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: It is shown how to ground scalar modifier meaning based on data collected from the Web and that meanings can be learned from Web data and that such meanings can drive pragmatic inference.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Methods for Numeracy-Preserving Word Embeddings
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: DICE outperforms a wide range of pre-trained word embedding models across multiple examples of two tasks: evaluating the ability to capture numeration and magnitude; and to perform list maximum, decoding, and addition.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Visual sense of number vs. sense of magnitude in humans and machines
recs.summary: Deep neural networks are tested on the same numerosity comparison task that was administered to human participants, using a stimulus space that allows the precise measurement of the contribution of non-numerical features, suggesting that numerosity is a major, salient property of the authors' visual environment.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Numeracy-600K: Learning Numeracy for Detecting Exaggerated Information in Market Comments
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper attempts to answer the question of whether neural network models can learn numeracy, which is the ability to predict the magnitude of a numeral at some specific position in a text description, through comprehensive experiments.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: An Empirical Investigation of Contextualized Number Prediction
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A suite of output distribution parameterizations are introduced that incorporate latent variables to add expressivity and better fit the natural distribution of numeric values in running text, and combine them with both recur-rent and transformer-based encoder architectures.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Learning Numeral Embedding
recs.summary: Two novel numeral embedding methods that can handle the out-of-vocabulary (OOV) problem for numerals are proposed and shown its effectiveness on four intrinsic and extrinsic tasks: word similarity, embedding numeracy, numeral prediction, and sequence labeling.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: “When Numbers Matter!”: Detecting Sarcasm in Numerical Portions of Text
recs.summary: This paper focuses on detecting sarcasm in tweets arising out of numbers, and implements a rule-based and a statistical machine learning-based (ML) classifier that conveys the crux of the numerical sarcasm problem, namely, incongruity arising in numbers.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: SemEval-2018 Task 5: Counting Events and Participants in the Long Tail
recs.summary: The design of this referential quantification task of counting events and participants in local, long-tail news documents with high ambiguity is detail, the participating systems are described, and additional analysis is presented to gain deeper insight into their performance.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Grounding Gradable Adjectives through Crowdsourcing
recs.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
recs.summary: A method is proposed for estimating concrete groundings for a set of gradable adjectives that can take a range of magnitudes such as small or slight using crowdsourcing to gather human language intuitions about the impact of each adjective and a linear mixed effects model to this data.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Dataset for Evaluation of Mathematical Reasoning Abilities in Russian
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: A Fact-aligned Corpus of Numerical Expressions
recs.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
recs.summary: A corpus of numerical expressions developed as part of the NUMGEN project is described, showing that when a fact is mentioned more than once in a text, there is a clear tendency for precision to increase from first to subsequent mentions, and for mathematical level either to remain constant or to increase.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision
